chunks: Abu Ahmad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us: He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Humran al-Qishiri narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Jarish Ahmad ibn Isa al-Kilabi narrated to us: Musa ibn Ismail ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated in the year 250 (AH): My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him).

Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?' Ali (peace be upon him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and High, said: What is the reward for one whom I have blessed with the best but Paradise?'

key_terms.الْإِحْسَانُ: Goodness / Excellence in faith and action

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those blessed with divine unity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration within the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt to establish the theological principle that Tawhid (monotheism) is the foundational cause of Paradise, rather than merely a condition. This interpretation elevates the verse from Surah Ar-Rahman from a general statement of reciprocity to a specific divine promise linking the essence of faith directly to eternal bliss, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intrinsic value of divine knowledge and belief.
